claim: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common arrhythmia in humans, characterized by irregularly irregular atrial electrical activity, resulting in asynchronous atrial contraction.
source: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common arrhythmia in humans, characterized by irregularly irregular atrial electrical activity, resulting in asynchronous atrial contraction.
evidence: This is a definitional statement about AF that draws from established medical knowledge.

claim: AF affects more than 33 million people globally.
source: AF is a global problem, affecting more than 33 million people and approximately 25% of Americans over the age of forty (Nishida and Nattel, 2014; Weng et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Nishida and Nattel, 2014 and Weng et al., 2018.

claim: Approximately 25% of Americans over the age of forty are affected by AF.
source: AF is a global problem, affecting more than 33 million people and approximately 25% of Americans over the age of forty (Nishida and Nattel, 2014; Weng et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Nishida and Nattel, 2014 and Weng et al., 2018.

claim: AF is associated with significant morbidity and mortality due to thromboembolic events, heart failure, and sudden cardiac death.
source: AF is associated with significant morbidity and mortality due to thromboembolic events, heart failure, and sudden cardiac death.
evidence: This is a statement of established medical knowledge about AF complications.

claim: AF patients cost five times more to treat than patients without AF.
source: AF also significantly complicates overall health care management, with AF patients costing five times more to treat than patients without AF (Andrade et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Andrade et al., 2014.

claim: The total annual cost to treat AF patients in the US is on the order of 26 billion dollars.
source: The total annual cost to treat AF patients in the US is on the order of 26 billion dollars (Nishida and Nattel, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Nishida and Nattel, 2014.

claim: Heritability provides between 40% and 62% of AF risk.
source: Large community-based cohort studies indicate that heritability provides between 40% and 62% of AF risk (Nishida and Nattel, 2014; Christophersen et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Nishida and Nattel, 2014 and Christophersen et al., 2009.

claim: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified common risk variants and familial mutations at the T-box transcription factor 5 (TBX5) locus that result in increased risk for AF.
source: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) studies have identified common risk variants and familial mutations at the T-box transcription factor 5 (TBX5) locus that result in increased risk for AF (McDermott et al., 2008; Sinner et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to McDermott et al., 2008 and Sinner et al., 2014.

claim: Adult-specific Tbx5 knockout mice demonstrate primary spontaneous and sustained AF.
source: Adult-specific Tbx5 knockout mice demonstrate primary spontaneous and sustained AF, providing evidence supporting the genetic implication at this locus.
evidence: This is a statement about the mouse model that is supported by the study's own data.

claim: GWAS have implicated multiple genes involved in cardiomyocyte calcium handling, including Atp2a2, Sln, and Pln.
source: GWAS have also implicated multiple genes involved in cardiomyocyte calcium handling, including Atp2a2, encoding the sarcolemmal calcium ATPase SERCA2, and Sln and Pln, encoding direct binding SERCA2 inhibitors sarcolipin and phospholamban, respectively.
evidence: This is a statement about GWAS findings that draws from established literature.

claim: Cardiomyocyte calcium control genes are direct TBX5 targets.
source: We have previously demonstrated that these cardiomyocyte calcium control genes are direct TBX5 targets (Nadadur et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Nadadur et al., 2016.

claim: Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 mice developed spontaneous AF as assessed by surface ECG compared to R26CreERT2.
source: Consistent with previous observations, the adult Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 but not control mice developed spontaneous AF, showing an irregularly irregular heartbeat, by telemetric electrocardiogram (ECG) recordings (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: Supported by ECG data shown in Figure 1A,B.

claim: APs and [Ca]i transients were prolonged in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2.
source: As previously shown, APs and [Ca]i transients were prolonged in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 (Figure 1C) (Nadadur et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by data in Figure 1C and citation to Nadadur et al., 2016.

claim: Ryr2 mRNA transcripts were decreased by 61% in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 mice compared to R26CreERT2 controls (p=0.026).
source: mRNA transcripts for RyR2 (Ryr2) and SERCA2 (Atp2a2), two of the main determinants of sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) calcium flux, were decreased by 61% and 71% respectively in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 mice compared to R26CreERT2 controls (p=0.026 and p=0.001 for Ryr2 and Atp2a2 respectively) consistent with previous studies (Nadadur et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data presented in the manuscript and citation to Nadadur et al., 2016.

claim: Atp2a2 mRNA transcripts were decreased by 71% in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 mice compared to R26CreERT2 controls (p=0.001).
source: mRNA transcripts for RyR2 (Ryr2) and SERCA2 (Atp2a2), two of the main determinants of sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) calcium flux, were decreased by 61% and 71% respectively in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 mice compared to R26CreERT2 controls (p=0.026 and p=0.001 for Ryr2 and Atp2a2 respectively) consistent with previous studies (Nadadur et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data presented in the manuscript and citation to Nadadur et al., 2016.

claim: Phospholamban (Pln) mRNA expression was increased by 69% in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 compared to R26CreERT2 (p=0.023).
source: In addition, phospholamban (Pln) mRNA expression was increased by 69% in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 compared to R26CreERT2 (p=0.023), which would be expected to further depress SERCA2 activity.
evidence: Supported by qPCR data presented in the manuscript.

claim: There was no significant difference in mRNA expression of Cacna1c, Ncx1, or calmodulins 1-3 between Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 and R26CreERT2.
source: There was no significant difference in mRNA expression of the alpha 1C subunit of the L-type calcium channel (Cacna1c), the cardiac sodium calcium exchanger (Ncx1), or any of the calmodulins 1–3 (Calm1, Calm2, Calm3) (Figure 1C).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1D (note: text says Figure 1C but refers to panel D).

claim: 30 μM nifedipine completely inhibited L-type calcium current in control R26CreERT2 and Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2.
source: 30 μM nifedipine completely inhibited L-type calcium current, preventing Ca2+ entry or release of SR calcium in control R26CreERT2 and Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: In control R26CreERT2 atrial cardiomyocytes, nifedipine caused 19 ± 4% shortening of APD90 (p=0.008).
source: In control R26CreERT2 atrial cardiomyocytes, the effect of nifedipine on AP duration (APD) was small, with 19 ± 4% shortening of APD at 90% repolarization (APD90) (p=0.008) (Figure 2A).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: In Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 atrial cardiomyocytes, nifedipine shortened APD50 by 16 ± 6% (p=0.02) and APD90 by 61 ± 6% (p=0.007).
source: However, in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 atrial cardiomyocytes, nifedipine had a profound effect: APD at 50% repolarization (APD50) was shortened by 16 ± 6% and APD90 by 61 ± 6% (p=0.02 and 0.007 respectively) (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B,C.

claim: Western blot with densitometry analysis for CaV1.2 showed no significant difference in protein expression between Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 and R26CreERT2.
source: Western blot with densitometry analysis for CaV1.2 showed no significant difference in protein expression (Figure 2D), in line with the qPCR data (Figure 1D), consistent with no TBX5-driven direct transcriptional regulation of L-type calcium channels.
evidence: Supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Peak ICaL current was increased 92 ± 34% (p=0.027) in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 atrial cardiomyocytes compared to control R26CreERT2.
source: However, peak ICaL current was increased 92 ± 34% (p=0.027) in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 atrial cardiomyocytes compared to control R26CreERT2 (Figure 2E and F).
evidence: Supported by voltage clamp data shown in Figure 2E and F.

claim: The inactivation kinetics at peak ICaL were accelerated in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 compared to control R26CreERT2 (τ = 26.7 ± 3.4 ms vs. τ = 40.0 ± 3.0 ms; p=0.05).
source: The inactivation kinetics at peak ICaL were accelerated Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 compared to control R26CreERT2 ( τ = 26.7 ± 3.4 ms vs. τ = 40.0 ± 3.0 ms; p=0.05).
evidence: Supported by analysis of ICaL kinetics from experimental data.

claim: Steady-state ICaL inactivation was unchanged between Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 and R26CreERT2.
source: Steady-state ICaL inactivation was unchanged (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: RyR2 protein expression was significantly decreased in left atria of Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 mice compared to R26CreERT2 mice.
source: RyR2 protein expression was significantly decreased in left atria of Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 mice compared to R26CreERT2 mice by western blot (Figure 3A), consistent with the observed downregulation of Ryr2 mRNA (Figure 1B).
evidence: Supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The frequency of Ca2+ sparks in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 atrial cardiomyocytes was decreased in comparison with R26CreERT2 atrial cardiomyocytes at different pacing frequencies from 0 to 2 Hz.
source: The frequency of Ca2+ sparks in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 atrial cardiomyocytes was decreased in comparison with R26CreERT2 atrial cardiomyocytes at different pacing frequencies from 0 to 2 Hz (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by confocal linescan data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Overall ryanodine binding was unchanged over the majority of the physiological range of calcium values in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 compared to R26CreERT2, with no shift in calcium sensitivity.
source: Despite reduced ryanodine receptor expression, overall ryanodine binding was unchanged over the majority of the physiological range of calcium values, with no shift in calcium sensitivity (Figure 3D).
evidence: Supported by [3H]-ryanodine binding assay data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: SERCA2 protein expression was decreased in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 compared to R26CreERT2 atria.
source: We observed that SERCA2 protein expression was decreased while NCX1 protein expression was increased in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 in comparison with R26CreERT2 atria (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: Supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: NCX1 protein expression was increased in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 compared to R26CreERT2 atria.
source: We observed that SERCA2 protein expression was decreased while NCX1 protein expression was increased in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 in comparison with R26CreERT2 atria (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: Supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: [Ca2+]i transient peaks were unchanged between Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 and R26CreERT2 atrial cardiomyocytes during field stimulation.
source: The [Ca2+]i transient peaks were unchanged, but [Ca2+]i transient decay rates, corresponding to SR Ca2+ uptake and cellular Ca2+ extrusion, were slowed in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 compared to R26CreERT2 atrial cardiomyocytes (Figure 4E,F) (Nadadur et al., 2016), consistent with defective Ca2+ removal from the cytosol.
evidence: Supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 4E and citation to Nadadur et al., 2016.

claim: [Ca2+]i transient decay rates were slowed in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 compared to R26CreERT2 atrial cardiomyocytes.
source: The [Ca2+]i transient peaks were unchanged, but [Ca2+]i transient decay rates, corresponding to SR Ca2+ uptake and cellular Ca2+ extrusion, were slowed in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 compared to R26CreERT2 atrial cardiomyocytes (Figure 4E,F) (Nadadur et al., 2016), consistent with defective Ca2+ removal from the cytosol.
evidence: Supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 4F and citation to Nadadur et al., 2016.

claim: In voltage clamp mode, [Ca2+]i transient peaks were decreased by 23 ± 4% (p=0.02) in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 cardiomyocytes compared to R26CreERT2.
source: Similar to the field stimulation experiments, [Ca2+]i transient decay rates were slowed, but [Ca2+]i transient peaks were decreased by 23 ± 4% (p=0.02) in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 cardiomyocytes compared to R26CreERT2, which suggests that AP prolongation is essential to maintaining peak twitch [Ca2+]i.
evidence: Supported by voltage clamp calcium imaging data.

claim: SR [Ca2+] was reduced by 24 ± 8% (p=0.0005) in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 compared with R26CreERT2 atrial cardiomyocytes.
source: SR [Ca2+] was reduced by 24 ± 8% (p=0.0005) in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 compared with R26CreERT2 atrial cardiomyocytes (Figure 4G).
evidence: Supported by caffeine-induced SR release measurements shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Peak SERCA activity was reduced by 31 ± 9% (p=0.006) in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 compared with R26CreERT2 atrial cardiomyocytes.
source: Peak SERCA activity was reduced by 31 ± 9% (p=0.006) in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 compared with R26CreERT2 atrial cardiomyocytes (Figure 4C,H).
evidence: Supported by SERCA activity measurements shown in Figure 4C,H.

claim: NCX activity was ~60% higher in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 in comparison with R26CreERT2 atrial cardiomyocytes.
source: NCX activity was ~60% higher in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 in comparison with R26CreERT2 atrial cardiomyocytes (Figure 4D,I).
evidence: Supported by NCX activity measurements shown in Figure 4D,I.

claim: PLN expression was significantly increased in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 compared with R26CreERT2 atria.
source: Western blot analysis showed that PLN expression was significantly increased in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 compared with R26CreERT2 atria (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: PLN phosphorylation at serine 16 was increased in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 compared to R26CreERT2.
source: In addition, PLN phosphorylation was also increased at serine 16 in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 compared to R26CreERT2.
evidence: Supported by Western blot analysis of phosphorylated PLN.

claim: Control Pln deficient mice (Pln-/-;R26CreERT2) had increased steady state SR load and SERCA activity relative to R26CreERT2.
source: Control Pln deficient mice (Pln-/-;R26CreERT2) had increased steady state SR load and SERCA activity relative to R26CreERT2 (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: Supported by SR load and SERCA activity measurements shown in Figure 5C,D.

claim: The decreased SR load and SERCA function observed in Tbx5 mutant mice (Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2) was converted to elevated SR load and SERCA function after the removal of Pln (Tbx5fl/fl;Pln-/-; R26CreERT2).
source: The decreased SR load and SERCA function observed in Tbx5 mutant mice (Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2) was converted to elevated SR load and SERCA function after the removal of Pln (Tbx5fl/fl;Pln-/-; R26CreERT2) (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: Supported by SR load and SERCA activity measurements shown in Figure 5C,D.

claim: In the setting of combined Tbx5;Pln deficiency, peak twitch calcium and tau twitch were normalized to R26CreERT2 values.
source: However, in the setting of combined Tbx5;Pln deficiency, peak twitch calcium and tau twitch were normalized to R26CreERT2 values (Figure 5E,F).
evidence: Supported by calcium transient measurements shown in Figure 5E,F.

claim: The prolonged AP duration observed in Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 was rescued in both Tbx5fl/fl;Pln+/-;R26CreERT2 and Tbx5fl/fl;Pln-/-;R26CreERT2 atrial cardiomyocytes (43 ± 10% and 38 ± 5% shorter than Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 respectively; p=0.01, 0.0007).
source: The prolonged AP duration observed Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 was rescued in both Tbx5fl/fl;Pln+/-;R26CreERT2 and Tbx5fl/fl;Pln-/-;R26CreERT2 atrial cardiomyocytes (43 ± 10% and 38 ± 5% shorter than Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2 respectively; p=0.01, 0.0007) (Figure 6D,E).
evidence: Supported by action potential recordings shown in Figure 6D,E.

claim: Significantly fewer EADs and DADs were observed in Tbx5fl/fl;Pln-/-;R26CreERT2 cardiomyocytes compared to Tbx5fl/fl;R26CreERT2.
source: Along with normalization of AP duration, we observed significantly fewer EADs and DADs in Tbx5fl/fl;Pln-/-;R26CreERT2 cardiomyocytes (Figure 6F).
evidence: Supported by action potential recordings and quantification shown in Figure 6F.

claim: All Tbx5fl/fl; R26CreERT2 mice (6/6) paced into AF.
source: All Tbx5fl/fl; R26CreERT2 mice (6/6) paced into AF, compared to none of the R26CreERT2 (0/5) or Pln-/-;R26CreERT2 littermate controls (0/7).
evidence: Supported by intracardiac burst pacing experiments.

claim: None of the R26CreERT2 (0/5) or Pln-/-;R26CreERT2 (0/7) littermate controls paced into AF.
source: All Tbx5fl/fl; R26CreERT2 mice (6/6) paced into AF, compared to none of the R26CreERT2 (0/5) or Pln-/-;R26CreERT2 littermate controls (0/7).
evidence: Supported by intracardiac burst pacing experiments.

claim: Only 1/11 of Tbx5fl/fl;Pln-/-;R26CreERT2 paced into AF.
source: Consistent with our hypothesis, AF susceptibility was significantly decreased in Tbx5; Pln compound knockouts: only 1/11 of Tbx5fl/fl;Pln-/-;R26CreERT2 paced into AF (Figure 7F).
evidence: Supported by intracardiac burst pacing experiments shown in Figure 7F.

claim: TBX5 is critical for cellular Ca2+ homeostasis.
source: We report that TBX5 is critical for cellular Ca2+ homeostasis, providing a molecular mechanism underlying the genetic implication of TBX5 in AF.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: Cardiomyocyte action potential (AP) abnormalities in Tbx5-deficient atrial cardiomyocytes are caused by a decreased sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) Ca2+ ATPase (SERCA2)-mediated SR calcium uptake.
source: We show that cardiomyocyte action potential (AP) abnormalities in Tbx5-deficient atrial cardiomyocytes are caused by a decreased sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) Ca2+ ATPase (SERCA2)-mediated SR calcium uptake which was balanced by enhanced trans-sarcolemmal calcium fluxes (calcium current and sodium/calcium exchanger), providing mechanisms for triggered activity.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: Decreased SERCA2-mediated SR calcium uptake was balanced by enhanced trans-sarcolemmal calcium fluxes (calcium current and sodium/calcium exchanger).
source: We show that cardiomyocyte action potential (AP) abnormalities in Tbx5-deficient atrial cardiomyocytes are caused by a decreased sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) Ca2+ ATPase (SERCA2)-mediated SR calcium uptake which was balanced by enhanced trans-sarcolemmal calcium fluxes (calcium current and sodium/calcium exchanger), providing mechanisms for triggered activity.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: The AP defects, cardiomyocyte ectopy, and AF caused by TBX5 deficiency were rescued by phospholamban removal, which normalized SERCA function.
source: The AP defects, cardiomyocyte ectopy, and AF caused by TBX5 deficiency were rescued by phospholamban removal, which normalized SERCA function.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: Depressed SERCA activity provides higher cytosolic calcium driving force for calcium extrusion from the cell via electrogenic inward INCX.
source: Instead, slowed SR calcium uptake from depressed SERCA activity provides higher cytosolic calcium driving force for calcium extrusion from the cell via electrogenic inward INCX.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental findings and understanding of calcium handling mechanisms.

claim: Increased NCX function coupled with prolonged [Ca2+]i transients drives increased inward INCX, providing additional depolarizing current during the AP, contributing to its prolongation.
source: Thus, increased NCX function coupled with prolonged [Ca2+]i transients, drives increased inward INCX, providing additional depolarizing current during the AP, contributing to its prolongation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental findings and understanding of NCX function.

claim: DADs can occur with depressed SR loads in the appropriate context of depressed SERCA and elevated NCX function.
source: Our data further support that DADs, which are classically thought to relate to SR calcium overload can still occur with depressed SR loads in the appropriate context of depressed SERCA and elevated NCX function (Voigt et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental findings and citation to Voigt et al., 2012.

claim: Compensatory increases in L-type calcium current in the setting of depressed SERCA function could be required to maintain systolic and diastolic calcium levels.
source: Modeling suggests that compensatory increases in L-type calcium current in the setting of depressed SERCA function could be required to maintain systolic and diastolic calcium levels (Li et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Li et al., 2011.

claim: The increase in calcium entering the cell through ICaL during the AP would be expected to balance a net increase in NCX mediated calcium extrusion, a requirement for steady state [Ca2+]i homeostasis.
source: Additionally, the increase in calcium entering the cell through ICaL during the AP would be expected to balance a net increase in NCX mediated calcium extrusion (Figure 4I), a requirement for steady state [Ca2+]i homeostasis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental findings and understanding of calcium homeostasis.

claim: L-type calcium channel expression is TBX5-independent.
source: However, our observations that L-type calcium channel expression is TBX5-independent (Figures 1D and 2D) and that genetically targeting only the Ca2+ efflux pathways in our model is sufficient to restore normal electrical activity (Figures 5–7) suggest that the ICaL change is not a primary TBX5-dependent effect.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental findings shown in Figures 1D, 2D, 5-7.

claim: Genetically targeting only the Ca2+ efflux pathways in the Tbx5 mutant model is sufficient to restore normal electrical activity.
source: However, our observations that L-type calcium channel expression is TBX5-independent (Figures 1D and 2D) and that genetically targeting only the Ca2+ efflux pathways in our model is sufficient to restore normal electrical activity (Figures 5–7) suggest that the ICaL change is not a primary TBX5-dependent effect.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental findings shown in Figures 5-7.

claim: RYR2 is a known susceptibility locus for AF.
source: RYR2 is a known susceptibility locus for AF and RYR2 mutations are correlated with AF (Fatkin et al., 2017; Di Pino et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Fatkin et al., 2017 and Di Pino et al., 2014.

claim: RYR2 mutations are correlated with AF.
source: RYR2 is a known susceptibility locus for AF and RYR2 mutations are correlated with AF (Fatkin et al., 2017; Di Pino et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Fatkin et al., 2017 and Di Pino et al., 2014.

claim: Defective RyR2 function has been associated with AF.
source: Defective RyR2 function has also been associated with AF (Vest et al., 2005; King et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Vest et al., 2005 and King et al., 2013.

claim: RyR2 function is generally preserved over the physiologic range of calcium in Tbx5-mutant atria despite TBX5-dependent RyR2 expression.
source: Despite TBX5-dependent RyR2 expression, the ryanodine binding assay (Xu et al., 1998) suggested that RyR2 function is generally preserved over the physiologic range of calcium in Tbx5-mutant atria (Figure 3D).
evidence: Supported by ryanodine binding assay data shown in Figure 3D and citation to Xu et al., 1998.

claim: Phospholamban has been associated with AF by GWAS.
source: While phospholamban has been associated with AF by GWAS (Fatkin et al., 2017; Federico et al., 2017), its functional role is less clear.
evidence: Supported by citations to Fatkin et al., 2017 and Federico et al., 2017.

claim: PLN participates in rheostatic control of SERCA activity in the atria, which is sufficient to protect against AF inducibility.
source: Although PLN is predominantly found in the ventricle (Bhupathy et al., 2007), we showed not only its expression is increased in the atria in the context of Tbx5 loss, but also PLN participates in rheostatic control of SERCA activity in the atria, which is sufficient to protect against AF inducibility (Figures 5–7).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental findings shown in Figures 5-7 and citation to Bhupathy et al., 2007.

claim: In patients who experience post-operative AF, SERCA2 is significantly decreased in the atrial tissue.
source: For example, in patients who experience post-operative AF, SERCA2 is significantly decreased in the atrial tissue (Zaman et al., 2016), but those with PLN mutations have decreased AF susceptibility in the context of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (Bourfiss et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zaman et al., 2016.

claim: Patients with PLN mutations have decreased AF susceptibility in the context of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
source: For example, in patients who experience post-operative AF, SERCA2 is significantly decreased in the atrial tissue (Zaman et al., 2016), but those with PLN mutations have decreased AF susceptibility in the context of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (Bourfiss et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bourfiss et al., 2016.

claim: In AF compounded by heart failure, decreased SERCA2 and phosphorylated PLN, and increased NCX1 expression were observed.
source: In AF compounded by heart failure, decreased SERCA2 and phosphorylated PLN, and increased NCX1 expression were observed (Lugenbiel et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lugenbiel et al., 2015.

claim: Decrease in phosphorylated PLN coupled with an increase in total PLN has been found in animal models of obesity, potentially increasing risk of AF.
source: Decrease in phosphorylated PLN coupled with an increase in total PLN has been found in animal models of obesity, potentially increasing risk of AF (Lima-Leopoldo et al., 2014; Lima-Leopoldo et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to Lima-Leopoldo et al., 2014 and Lima-Leopoldo et al., 2008.

claim: A selective NCX1 inhibitor, ORM-10103, was shown to prevent cellular Ca2+ handling abnormalities in ischemic ventricular cardiomyocytes.
source: For example, a selective NCX1 inhibitor, ORM-10103, was shown to prevent cellular Ca2+ handling abnormalities in ischemic ventricular cardiomyocytes, possibly by limiting calcium entry through outward INCX (Jost et al., 2013; Kormos et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Jost et al., 2013 and Kormos et al., 2014.

claim: Resveratrol, which increases SERCA2 activity, has been shown to decrease AF.
source: Further, resveratrol, which increases SERCA2 activity, has been shown to decrease AF, suggesting that targeting SERCA2 activity may be a viable therapeutic approach (Bai et al., 2016; Chong et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bai et al., 2016 and Chong et al., 2015.
